# **Autonomous Full-Stack Web Engineering: Video Deconstruction, End-to-End System Architecture, and Pre-Flight MCP Remediation for Google Antigravity**

## **Video Deconstruction and Workflow Forensics**

### **Triangulating the Source Video and Operational Thesis**

An examination of the specified technology stack—Google Antigravity orchestrating the Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for Google Stitch, Supabase, GitHub, and Vercel—identifies the core workflow demonstrated in the viral engineering tutorial *"Antigravity \+ Stitch MCP: AI Agents That Build Complete Websites"* (published by Code A Program) and its official Google Codelab counterpart, *"Design-to-Code with Antigravity and Stitch MCP"*, alongside the companion full-stack database and deployment tutorials (*"Easily Build A Database In Google Antigravity MCP \+ Supabase Tutorial"* and *"Full-Stack Vibe Coding: Building Production-Ready Apps with AI Studio, Stitch & Antigravity"*)1. Across these demonstrations, the central thesis is the transition from manual, fragmented software implementation to an "agent-first" development lifecycle2. Historically, user interface design and frontend or backend engineering operated in isolated silos, requiring manual translation from visual canvases such as Figma into React components, database schemas, and deployment pipelines5. The video workflow eliminates this translation tax by utilizing MCP as a universal, bidirectional bridge between an autonomous coding environment (Google Antigravity) and external cloud infrastructure3.  
In the primary video demonstration, the presenter constructs complete, multi-page web applications—specifically showcasing a SaaS space-tech platform named *PaperGen*, alongside live production demos for an E-commerce storefront and a Fitness tracking platform—without writing manual boilerplate code2. When extended with the full-stack companion workflows, the demonstrated application capabilities encompass high-converting landing pages, glassmorphic pricing tiers, interactive analytics dashboards with paginated data tables, real-time order and status tracking, user authentication, persistent cloud database storage, and one-click cloud deployment3. Looking forward, this convergence signals an industry shift toward AI-aware design systems and autonomous delivery harnesses where human engineers govern declarative specifications rather than imperative syntax5.

### **Frame-by-Frame Deconstruction of the Demonstrated Workflow**

The video narrative progresses through six distinct operational phases that transform a raw text concept into a live web application3. During the initial visual source-of-truth generation phase, the workflow begins outside the code editor inside Google Stitch (stitch.withgoogle.com), an AI-native UI design canvas unveiled at Google I/O 2025 and powered by Gemini 3 and Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash models3. Selecting the "Web" project toggle to optimize for browser-based layouts and choosing the Gemini 3 model for advanced layout generation, the operator submits a structured aesthetic prompt requesting a midnight blue and neon purple SaaS interface for a space-tech startup called PaperGen, featuring a hero section with a "Get Started" button, a three-column features grid, and a glassmorphism pricing table3. Stitch synthesizes the visual screens, which the operator names PaperGen in the top header and refines via conversational sidebar prompts or design variant exploration3.  
Following visual ideation, the workflow moves into credential provisioning and MCP bridging3. The operator generates a dedicated API key within the Stitch settings panel and opens the Google Antigravity IDE3. Accessing the Agent Manager via keyboard shortcuts (CMD+E on macOS or CTRL+E on Windows), the operator initializes a local workspace directory (PaperGen-Project) and installs the Stitch integration from the built-in MCP Store, binding the API key to the server configuration3. The connection is validated by prompting the agent to list active Stitch projects, which triggers the list\_projects MCP tool over Streamable HTTP and confirms the presence of PaperGen3.  
Once connectivity is verified, the operator initiates semantic Design DNA extraction3. Rather than feeding static screenshots to the coding model—an anti-pattern that degrades layout accuracy—the operator instructs Antigravity to fetch the underlying design data directly3. The agent invokes Stitch MCP tools (get\_project, list\_screens, get\_screen) to parse the HTML and CSS structure, color hex codes, and typography, compiling them into a standardized DESIGN.md specification file in the repository root3.  
With DESIGN.md established as a semantic contract in the project root, the workflow transitions to autonomous full-stack scaffolding3. The operator commands Antigravity to build the full website using modular React and Tailwind CSS components3. Utilizing google-labs-code/stitch-skills and terminal execution tools, the agent scaffolds the project structure, decouples static design content into external mock data files, converts raw Stitch HTML into reusable React components (such as Sidebar, Header, Stats Cards, and Pricing Table), and launches the local development server3.  
After scaffolding, the agent opens the running application inside Antigravity's integrated browser for visual verification, a stage referred to in the tutorial ecosystem as the "Vibe Check"3. When visual discrepancies appear—such as misaligned button padding or incorrect font weights on the "Get Started" button—the operator issues a natural language correction3. The agent re-queries the Stitch MCP server to cross-reference the original screen specification and patches the Tailwind utility classes in the codebase autonomously3.  
In the final stage, the frontend prototype is elevated into a production system using the broader MCP ecosystem for database persistence, version control, and cloud deployment1. The Supabase MCP server provisions PostgreSQL tables, applies schema migrations (apply\_migration), generates TypeScript definitions (generate\_typescript\_types), and configures user authentication1. Simultaneously, the GitHub MCP server commits the modular codebase and manages pull requests, while the Vercel MCP server links the repository, injects environment variables, triggers production builds, and monitors deployment logs15.

## **End-to-End Software Architecture for the Unified PaperGen Platform**

### **Functional Scope and Dual-Plane Product Definition**

To ensure that every task demonstrated in the video tutorials and supported by the underlying MCP servers can be executed directly within the web application itself, the system is architected as a **Dual-Plane SaaS and Autonomous Web Studio Platform** named **PaperGen OmniStudio**. A standard marketing website only fulfills the static UI portion of the video; by contrast, a dual-plane architecture satisfies both the *product templates* showcased in the video (SaaS landing page, E-commerce storefront, Fitness and Analytics dashboard)2 and the *agentic orchestration capabilities* of the toolset (design generation, database exploration, repository management, and deployment automation)8.  
**Plane A (The Commercial SaaS & Transactional Portal)** delivers the public and customer-facing web experience demonstrated in the Stitch Codelab and live demo sites2. It includes the midnight-blue and neon-purple Hero showcase, a dynamic three-column feature and product catalog grid, a glassmorphism pricing and subscription checkout engine, multi-provider social authentication (Google and GitHub OAuth with "Remember me" session persistence), and a responsive dark-mode customer dashboard featuring real-time order and project status tracking alongside recommendation carousels3.  
**Plane B (The Embedded Agentic Control Plane & Workspace)** empowers authenticated users on the website to perform all AI design, database, and DevOps tasks directly from their browser8. It embeds an AI UI Generator Studio (interfacing with the @google/stitch-sdk to generate screens from text prompts, edit existing screens, and spin up design variants)8, an Interactive Database Explorer (utilizing mcp-use React 19 widgets for visual schema browsing, sortable data tables, and read-only SQL query execution)9, a Custom Edge MCP Server (built with mcp-lite on Supabase Edge Functions so external AI clients can query the platform)23, and a Live DevOps Telemetry Console (interfacing with GitHub and Vercel APIs to trigger builds, manage custom domains, and stream runtime logs)16.

### **Frontend Component Architecture and Design Token Enforcement**

The frontend layer is engineered on **Next.js (App Router) with React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI primitives, and Lucide React icons**5. This exact combination aligns with both the Vercel MCP Fluid Compute runtime requirements (Node.js 20+) and the mcp-use interactive React widget architecture for Supabase9. Rather than hardcoding arbitrary hex values across components, the frontend build pipeline consumes the root DESIGN.md file—open-sourced by Google under the Apache 2.0 license in April 2026—and compiles its nine standard sections into W3C Design Tokens and CSS custom variables (--color-midnight-base, \--color-neon-purple, \--glass-blur, \--radius-card) injected directly into tailwind.config.ts3.

To support the embedded mcp-use React 19 database widgets (schema-explorer, table-viewer, and query-results) without triggering browser security blocks, the Next.js application middleware must explicitly configure Content Security Policy (CSP) headers allowing frames and connections from https\://supabase.com, https\://mcp.supabase.com, https\://\*.mcp-use.com, and https\://\*.supabase.co9.

### **Backend Database Schema, Row-Level Security, and Edge MCP Layer**

The persistence and serverless compute tier is hosted on **Supabase**, combining a managed PostgreSQL database, PostgREST data APIs, Realtime database broadcast channels, and Deno 2.1 Edge Functions14. To support both Plane A and Plane B operations securely in a multi-tenant environment, the relational schema is partitioned across six core tables governed by strict PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies14. At the identity root, public.organizations and public.profiles link via foreign key to auth.users, storing tenant workspaces, role-based access levels (owner, admin, editor, viewer), encrypted user preferences, and billing tier quotas4. Application metadata is persisted within public.projects, which tracks unified projects created by users, storing the internal project\_slug, linked stitch\_project\_id, github\_repo\_url, vercel\_project\_id, and the versioned markdown text of the project's DESIGN.md specification3.  
Visual artifacts generated through Plane B are recorded in public.design\_screens, which stores individual UI screens and variants synthesized via the Stitch API, including stitch\_screen\_id, prompt\_text, model\_used (enumerated for gemini-3, gemini-2.5-pro, or gemini-2.5-flash), raw\_html, react\_code, and viewport\_type across desktop, tablet, and mobile targets3. Simultaneously, public.commerce\_orders supports the commercial e-commerce and SaaS subscription workflows demonstrated in the live demo sites by recording customer transactions, pricing tier selections, and real-time fulfillment status2. Finally, public.deployment\_logs archives build telemetry, Vercel deployment identifiers, Git commit SHAs, web vitals metrics (send\_web\_vitals), and automated security advisor reports (get\_advisors)14.  
Beyond serving standard web traffic, the backend exposes two distinct MCP interfaces of its own so that external AI assistants can interact with the hosted platform23. First, the Next.js Fluid Compute MCP Endpoint (/api/mcp/route.ts) is built using Vercel's mcp-handler (v2.x), @modelcontextprotocol/server, and zod running on Node.js 20 or later24. Wrapped with withMcpAuth, this endpoint exposes project search, design token retrieval, and deployment status tools over Streamable HTTP to external AI clients such as ChatGPT (in developer mode), Claude, or Cursor24. Second, the Supabase Edge Function MCP Server (/functions/mcp-server/index.ts) is constructed with mcp-lite, a lightweight, zero-dependency TypeScript framework running on Deno 2 with a per\_worker isolation policy for millisecond cold starts23. Mounted via app.route('/mcp-server', mcpApp) to accommodate Supabase's root routing structure and secured with withOAuthProtectedResource and withSupabase from @supabase/server, it uses Supabase Auth as an OAuth 2.1 authorization server so every external tool call (searchDatabase, exportDesignTokens, triggerBuild) executes strictly under the signed-in user's RLS permissions23.

### **Repository Topology and Serverless Deployment Pipeline**

The codebase is organized as a strict, modular monorepo-style Next.js workspace that cleanly separates agent instructions from application runtime code7. This structural separation ensures that local coding agents in Antigravity can discover workspace rules and skills without bundling configuration metadata into client-side JavaScript bundles29.

| Directory / File Path | Architectural Purpose | Governing Agent / Runtime |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| /DESIGN.md | 9-section Apache 2.0 semantic design contract defining palette, typography, spacing, and component states3. | Read by Antigravity & Stitch MCP; compiled to Tailwind tokens6. |
| /AGENTS.md & /GEMINI.md | Natural language engineering standards, architectural boundaries, and SQL/API guardrails29. | Loaded at startup by Antigravity IDE and CLI (agy)30. |
| /.agents/mcp\_config.json | Workspace-scoped MCP server registry defining Stitch, Supabase, GitHub, Vercel, and Playwright endpoints7. | Discovered automatically by Antigravity IDE, CLI, and Python SDK7. |
| /.agents/plugin.json & /hooks.json | Self-contained Antigravity plugin manifest and deterministic lifecycle hook scripts (PreToolUse, Stop)29. | Executed outside the LLM reasoning loop by Antigravity runtime29. |
| /skills/\*/SKILL.md | Modular procedural playbooks (e.g., stitch-react-converter, supabase-rls-auditor, vercel-log-triage)13. | Loaded via progressive disclosure or /skill-name slash commands29. |
| /src/app/api/mcp/route.ts | Hosted Streamable HTTP MCP connector using mcp-handler v2 and withMcpAuth24. | Executed on Vercel Fluid Compute (Node.js 20+)24. |
| /supabase/functions/mcp-server/ | Edge MCP server powered by mcp-lite and Deno 2.1 with OAuth 2.1 RLS scoping23. | Executed on Supabase global Edge Functions runtime23. |
| /supabase/migrations/\*.sql | Version-controlled declarative DDL schemas, RLS policies, and database triggers14. | Applied via Supabase MCP apply\_migration tool14. |

## **Critical Gap Analysis of the Standard Video Workflow**

### **Architectural and Operational Deficiencies in Naive Vibe Coding**

While the video tutorials demonstrate rapid prototyping—transforming a text prompt into a styled React interface in minutes4—a rigorous software engineering audit reveals **seven critical deficiencies** in the standard workflow. Executing the raw tutorial steps without structural remediation leads to brittle codebases, security vulnerabilities, context window collapse, and failed production deployments.  
The first deficiency is semantic drift and the non-enforcement of DESIGN.md6. The video workflow treats DESIGN.md as an automatic compiler that guarantees pixel-perfect output3. In reality, DESIGN.md operates as a semantic guidance contract rather than a deterministic compiler or enforcement layer6. Without automated CSS linters, Tailwind token binding, and visual regression checks, coding agents gradually drift away from the specified hex codes and glassmorphism parameters during multi-turn component refactoring3.  
A second vulnerability involves context window pollution, monolithic prompts, and CLI replay echoes5. In tutorial demonstrations, operators frequently attempt to generate, convert, and wire an entire application in a single massive prompt, or load dozens of tool definitions simultaneously5. Practitioner post-mortems confirm that attempting everything in one prompt causes severe structural degradation compared to a disciplined Design → Code → Refactor sequence5. Furthermore, loading full tool manuals into the system prompt exhausts token budgets unless Antigravity's progressive disclosure (SKILL.md) and /compress (or /clear) CLI commands are utilized29. Additionally, when resuming multi-turn sessions in Antigravity CLI (agy) print mode (ask-antigravity), a known architectural quirk causes the CLI to replay the previous assistant message before the new response; while the MCP wrapper automatically strips replayed prefixes under 1,000 characters, longer responses leave a leading echo that corrupts downstream JSON parsing31.  
The third major risk centers on destructive database mutations and missing Row-Level Security (RLS)14. Connecting the Supabase MCP server with an unrestricted personal access token grants the coding agent broad administrative privileges across more than 20 tools (execute\_sql, apply\_migration, delete\_branch, pause\_project)14. Naive prompts instructing the agent to build backend tables routinely result in tables created in the public schema without Row-Level Security enabled, exposing all database records via the client-side anon key14. Moreover, running unattended or batch routines (batch-antigravity or bg-antigravity), which default to \--dangerously-skip-permissions (skipPermissions: true) because print mode cannot answer interactive prompts, allows an unguided agent to execute destructive SQL queries without human confirmation14.  
Fourth, standard tutorials exhibit plaintext secret exposure and confused deputy vulnerabilities10. Operators routinely paste API keys (STITCH\_API\_KEY, SUPABASE\_ACCESS\_TOKEN, VERCEL\_TOKEN) directly into chat prompts or commit them into workspace .json files10. Pasting secrets into chat logs leaks credentials into model context history10. Specifically for Supabase Edge Functions, passing secret values to the AI assistant violates the create\_edge\_function\_secret security design, which requires requesting only the secret name and using a secure Supabase Dashboard elicitation URL to enter the value14. Similarly, using the GitHub Copilot Coding Agent alongside Antigravity without prefixing repository secrets with COPILOT\_MCP\_ causes silent authentication failures against remote servers like Stitch12.  
Fifth, the demonstrated workflow suffers from the absence of automated browser verification and visual QA3. The Codelab relies on a manual human "Vibe Check" inside the integrated browser to spot padding or alignment defects3. This manual loop does not scale across the three verified viewports (desktop, tablet, and mobile) and leaves form submissions, OAuth redirects, and responsive breakpoints untested10. Integrating the Playwright MCP server is essential so the agent can autonomously launch a real browser, navigate routes, fill forms, capture DOM screenshots, and verify layout metrics before concluding a turn15.  
Sixth, protocol era fragmentation and filesystem traversal hazards threaten runtime stability32. As of the 2026-07-28 MCP specification revision, the protocol transitioned to stateless server/discover requests carrying protocol version, identity, and capabilities per request (introducing requestState, subscriptions/listen, cache hints, and JSON Schema 2020-12 tool schemas), while deprecating 2025-11-25 stateful initialize handshakes, ping, roots, sampling, and logging35. Additionally, Supabase's official MCP server does not send structuredContent in tool results32, and reference filesystem and git MCP servers have documented issues regarding unconfined repository scopes, symlink metadata leakage, parent-directory swap bugs on Windows, and NTFS alternate-data-stream paths (file:stream) if not explicitly confined37.  
Finally, the seventh deficiency involves Stitch generation quota exhaustion and single-tool round-trip bottlenecks3. Google Stitch's free tier enforces strict monthly ceilings: **350 generations per month** in Standard Mode (Gemini 2.5 Flash) and only **50 generations per month** in Experimental Mode (Gemini 2.5 Pro)11. When an unthrottled coding agent enters an autonomous retry loop calling generate\_screen\_from\_text for minor CSS adjustments—instead of modifying local Tailwind classes or utilizing Tier 4 compound SDK workflows (generate\_and\_extract, compare\_themes)—it rapidly exhausts the 50-generation Pro quota3.

## **Architectural Improvements and Pre-Flight Hardening Blueprint**

### **Converting Loose Prompts into a Deterministic Antigravity Plugin**

Rather than issuing ad-hoc conversational prompts to an unconfigured agent, the pre-flight remediation packages the entire engineering workflow into a versioned, self-contained **Antigravity Plugin** defined by a plugin.json manifest29. An Antigravity plugin unifies five extensibility primitives—**Skills** (SKILL.md), **MCP Servers** (mcp.json or mcp\_config.json), **Rules** (rules/AGENTS.md), **Hooks** (hooks.json), and **Custom Subagents** (agents/\<agent-name\>.md)—into a single deterministic unit29.  
To eliminate context window bloat, the architecture leverages Antigravity's **progressive disclosure** mechanism for Skills: at session startup, only each skill's name and concise description are loaded into the model's context window, while the exhaustive multi-step procedures, reference documentation, and helper scripts inside SKILL.md are pulled into context on demand only when relevant to the prompt or when invoked via a /skill-name slash command (such as /stitch-to-react, /supabase-rls-migrate, or /vercel-deploy-verify)29. Furthermore, complex implementation tasks are delegated to specialized Custom Subagents running in isolated context windows and separate git worktrees (delegate-antigravity), preventing frontend HTML extraction noise from polluting backend SQL migration context29.  
Crucially, **Lifecycle Hooks (hooks.json)** execute deterministic shell scripts *outside* the AI model's reasoning loop at six defined execution checkpoints: SessionStart, PreInvocation, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostInvocation, and Stop29. Because these hooks exchange structured JSON over standard input and output, they act as an unbypassable AST and runtime circuit breaker29. At SessionStart, the hook script verifies that DESIGN.md, environment variables, and required Node.js (v20+) and Python (v3.11+) runtimes are available in the workspace10. During PreToolUse, the interceptor inspects outgoing MCP tool payloads before execution, blocking any supabase/execute\_sql or supabase/apply\_migration call that contains destructive DDL (DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE) or CREATE TABLE statements lacking ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, while also throttling stitch/generate\_screen\_from\_text calls if the prompt only requests a minor CSS adjustment11. Immediately following tool execution, the PostToolUse hook automatically invokes supabase/generate\_typescript\_types after any database migration, redacts any accidental credential strings from tool outputs, and formats generated React components against the DESIGN.md Tailwind token linter6. Finally, at the Stop checkpoint, the gate script prevents the agent from finishing its turn until npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run test (Vitest), supabase/get\_advisors (verifying zero exposed tables or missing indexes), and Playwright MCP viewport assertions pass without error8.

### **Production-Ready Configuration Artifacts**

Before instructing Google Antigravity to build the website, the following four configuration files must be saved in the local workspace directory (PaperGen-Project)3. These artifacts establish the MCP server bridges, granular tool permission policies, semantic design tokens, persistent coding rules, and deterministic lifecycle hooks6.

#### **1\. Workspace MCP Server Configuration (/.agents/mcp\_config.json)**

Antigravity loads workspace-specific MCP definitions from /.agents/mcp\_config.json (and global definitions from \~/.gemini/config/mcp\_config.json)7. This configuration connects the official remote Streamable HTTP servers for Google Stitch, Supabase (scoped to the target project via project\_ref), and Vercel, alongside the local stdio servers for Vercel Administrative control, GitHub, Playwright (for automated multi-viewport browser QA), and the confined workspace Filesystem server7. Read-only discovery tools are pre-authorized under the allow policy, whereas state-mutating tools are gated under ask mode to require explicit confirmation7.

JSON

    "stitch": {  
      "type": "http",  
      "url": "https\://stitch.googleapis.com/mcp",  
      "headers": {  
        "Accept": "application/json",  
        "X-Goog-Api-Key": "\${STITCH\_API\_KEY}"  
      }  
    },  
    "supabase": {  
      "type": "http",

      }

      "mcp(supabase/list\_migrations)",  
      "mcp(supabase/get\_advisors)",  
      "mcp(supabase/query\_logs)",  
      "mcp(supabase/get\_project\_url)",  
      "mcp(supabase/get\_publishable\_keys)",  
      "mcp(supabase/generate\_typescript\_types)",  
      "mcp(vercel/\*)",  
      "mcp(playwright/\*)",  
      "mcp(filesystem/\*)"  
    \],  
    "ask": \[  
      "mcp(stitch/create\_project)",  
      "mcp(stitch/generate\_screen\_from\_text)",  
      "mcp(supabase/apply\_migration)",  
      "mcp(supabase/execute\_sql)",  
      "mcp(supabase/deploy\_edge\_function)",  
      "mcp(supabase/create\_edge\_function\_secret)",  
      "mcp(vercel-admin/\*)",  
      "mcp(github/\*)"  
    \]  
  }  
}

#### **2\. Semantic Design Specification (/DESIGN.md)**

Placed in the repository root, this file follows the nine-section Apache 2.0 DESIGN.md specification to provide a deterministic source of visual truth for both Stitch and Antigravity3.

# **DESIGN.md — PaperGen OmniStudio Design System Specification (v1.0)**

## **1\. Brand Identity & Aesthetic Direction**

Product Name: PaperGen OmniStudio. Domain: Next-Generation Space-Tech SaaS & Autonomous Web Engineering Portal. Aesthetic Persona: Deep Orbital Glassmorphism featuring high-contrast midnight backgrounds paired with luminous neon purple accents, crisp translucent surfaces, and precision telemetry typography.

## **2\. Color Palette & W3C Design Tokens**

Background Primary (--bg-midnight-950): \#060814. Background Elevated (--bg-midnight-900): \#0D1226. Glass Surface (--surface-glass): rgba(19, 27, 56, 0.65) with backdrop-filter blur(16px). Accent Primary (--accent-neon-purple): \#8B5CF6. Accent Secondary (--accent-cyber-cyan): \#06B6D4. Text Primary (--text-primary): \#F8FAFC. Text Muted (--text-secondary): \#94A3B8. Semantic Status: Success \#10B981, Warning \#F59E0B, Danger \#EF4444.

## **3\. Typography & Hierarchy**

Display & Headings (--font-display): Space Grotesk, weights 600 and 700, tracking \-0.02em. Body & UI Controls (--font-sans): Inter, weights 400, 500, and 600\. Code, SQL & Logs (--font-mono): JetBrains Mono, weight 400\. Scale: Hero H1 3.5rem (56px), Section H2 2.25rem (36px), Card Title H3 1.25rem (20px), Body 1rem (16px), Micro/Badge 0.75rem (12px).

## **4\. Layout Grid & Verified Viewports**

Desktop Viewport (1440px): 12-column CSS Grid, max-width 1280px, gap 24px, padding 32px. Tablet Viewport (768px): 8-column CSS Grid, collapsible sidebar drawer, gap 16px, padding 24px. Mobile Viewport (390px): Single-column stack, bottom navigation bar, gap 16px, padding 16px.

## **5\. Elevation, Borders & Glassmorphism Rules**

Card Border: 1px solid rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.25) transitioning to rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.65) on hover. Corner Radii: Outer containers 16px (rounded-2xl), inner controls and buttons 8px (rounded-lg), status pills 9999px (rounded-full). Glow Shadow: 0 8px 32px \-4px rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.18).

## **6\. Core Component Specifications (Plane A)**

Hero Section: Full-viewport header with animated orbital badge, dual CTA group (Get Started primary neon button and Launch Studio glass button), and live telemetry preview frame. Features Grid: 3-column symmetrical layout with icon badges, title, and concise metric callouts. Glassmorphism Pricing Table: 3-tier comparison matrix (Starter, Pro, Enterprise) with monthly/annual toggle and highlighted middle tier (border-purple-500). Customer Dashboard: Left collapsible sidebar (260px), top 4-card KPI row, main sortable/paginated data table, and real-time status drawer.

## **7\. Embedded Studio Component Specifications (Plane B)**

Stitch UI Synthesizer: Split-pane prompt editor and live iframe preview with desktop, tablet, and mobile viewport switches. Supabase Data Inspector: Embedded mcp-use React 19 widgets (schema-explorer, table-viewer, query-results) styled with Radix UI and dark theme variables. DevOps Deployment Console: Real-time log terminal (JetBrains Mono) and Vercel deployment status timeline.

## **8\. Interactive States & Micro-Interactions**

Buttons: px-6 py-3 standard padding, transition-all duration-200, active scale 0.98, focus ring 2px offset \#8B5CF6. Loading States: Shimmer skeleton placeholders matching exact component dimensions with zero layout shift (CLS \< 0.05).

## **9\. Accessibility & Compliance Guardrails**

Contrast: Minimum WCAG AA (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large headings and UI boundaries). Keyboard & ARIA: Full Radix UI keyboard navigation, focus traps on modals, and prefers-reduced-motion media query support.

#### **3\. Workspace Guardrails and Coding Standards (/rules/AGENTS.md)**

Read automatically by Antigravity IDE and CLI, this file establishes persistent engineering constraints across all agent turns29.

# **AGENTS.md — Operational Guardrails & Architectural Standards**

## **1\. Execution Methodology (Design \-\> Code \-\> Verify)**

Never attempt to scaffold the entire application in a single monolithic turn. Execute strictly in modular phases: Phase 1 (Design DNA & Token Setup), Phase 2 (Supabase Schema & RLS Migrations), Phase 3 (Plane A Commercial UI Components), Phase 4 (Plane B Studio SDK & Widget Integration), and Phase 5 (Playwright Verification & Vercel Deployment). Between major phases, invoke /compress to keep context noise minimal.

## **2\. Google Stitch MCP Usage & Quota Conservation**

Treat /DESIGN.md as the immutable visual contract. Map all colors, fonts, and radii into tailwind.config.ts CSS variables before creating React components. Conserve Stitch Experimental Mode quotas (limited to 50 generations per month on Gemini 2.5 Pro). Use Stitch MCP (generate\_screen\_from\_text) only for net-new screen layouts. For padding, alignment, or responsive fixes, modify local Tailwind CSS classes directly and verify via Playwright MCP.

## **3\. Supabase MCP Security & Database Hygiene**

Every table created in the public schema MUST include ALTER TABLE public.\<table\_name\> ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; and explicit CREATE POLICY statements for SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE scoped to auth.uid(). Never use raw execute\_sql for structural schema changes; always use apply\_migration so migrations are tracked versionally in /supabase/migrations/. Immediately after any apply\_migration call, invoke generate\_typescript\_types and write the output to /src/types/database.types.ts, then invoke get\_advisors to confirm zero security or performance warnings. Never request or accept raw secret values in chat. When configuring Edge Function secrets, call create\_edge\_function\_secret with the secret name only and instruct the operator to input the value via the Supabase Dashboard elicitation URL.

## **4\. Next.js, Edge MCP, and CSP Requirements**

Use Next.js App Router (Node.js 20+), React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, and Zod validation for all inputs. Configure next.config.mjs Content Security Policy headers to permit https\://supabase.com, https\://mcp.supabase.com, https\://*.mcp-use.com, and https\://*.supabase.co for interactive mcp-use database widgets. Implement /src/app/api/mcp/route.ts using mcp-handler v2 and withMcpAuth, and /supabase/functions/mcp-server/index.ts using mcp-lite with withOAuthProtectedResource and withSupabase.

#### **4\. Deterministic Lifecycle Hooks (/hooks.json)**

This configuration wires deterministic shell checks outside the model's reasoning loop to prevent destructive actions and enforce verification gates29.

JSON  
{  
  "hooks": {  
    "SessionStart": \[  
      {  
        "command": "node ./scripts/hooks/verify-env-and-design-md.mjs",  
        "description": "Verify Node \>= 20, DESIGN.md presence, and required MCP environment variables without logging secret values."  
      }  
    \],  
    "PreToolUse": \[  
      {  
        "matcher": "mcp(supabase/apply\_migration)\|mcp(supabase/execute\_sql)",  
        "command": "node ./scripts/hooks/sql-rls-circuit-breaker.mjs",  
        "description": "Parse SQL payload via AST; block DROP/TRUNCATE statements and reject CREATE TABLE statements lacking ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY."  
      },  
      {  
        "matcher": "mcp(github/\*)",  
        "command": "node ./scripts/hooks/secret-scanner.mjs",  
        "description": "Scan staged diffs for accidental API key or token strings before allowing GitHub commits or PR creation."  
      }  
    \],  
    "PostToolUse": \[  
      {  
        "matcher": "mcp(supabase/apply\_migration)",  
        "command": "npx supabase gen types typescript \--linked \> src/types/database.types.ts",  
        "description": "Synchronize TypeScript database definitions immediately after schema migration."  
      }  
    \],  
    "Stop": \[  
      {  
        "command": "npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test \-- \--run",  
        "description": "Require zero ESLint, TypeScript, and Vitest errors before allowing the agent to finish an implementation turn."  
      }  
    \]  
  }  
}

## **Conclusions and Master Execution Roadmap**

Transitioning from an impressive video demonstration to a resilient, production-grade web platform requires bridging the gap between probabilistic "vibe coding" and deterministic software engineering4. By synthesizing the visual ideation speed of Google Stitch with the multi-server orchestration of Google Antigravity, Supabase, GitHub, and Vercel—and hardening that pipeline through a Dual-Plane architecture, DESIGN.md token compilation, RLS-enforced PostgreSQL schemas, and hooks.json circuit breakers—an engineering team eliminates the fragile failure modes of naive agentic builds6.  
With the pre-flight files (/.agents/mcp\_config.json, /DESIGN.md, /rules/AGENTS.md, and /hooks.json) saved in the workspace, the operator executes the complete build by feeding five sequential phase prompts into the Google Antigravity IDE or CLI (agy), waiting for each phase's deterministic verification gate to pass and running /compress between phases to maintain a clean context window3.
